meta.drug: low-dose methotrexate (Trexall; target 15-20 mg weekly, plus folic acid 1 mg daily)
meta.sponsor: Brigham and Women's Hospital (investigator-initiated), funded by the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI)
meta.mechanism: folate antagonist (dihydrofolate reductase inhibitor); at low dose its anti-inflammatory effect is thought to be adenosine-mediated; no effect on lipids or blood pressure; not a direct inhibitor of the IL-1beta / IL-6 / CRP pathway
meta.indication: secondary prevention in stable patients with prior myocardial infarction or multivessel coronary disease plus type 2 diabetes or the metabolic syndrome (no hsCRP entry criterion)

n_randomized.quote: At the time the trial was terminated, 4786 of the 6158 eligible patients had completed the run-in phase and had been randomly assigned to either low-dose methotrexate (2391 patients) or placebo (2395 patients)
n_randomized.note: Planned 7000 (S5), reduced to 5500 in 2018 (S1). Registry S4 enrollment 4786 (actual). Data from a small cluster of sites with Good Clinical Practice violations were excluded before unblinding (S1).

median_followup.quote: After a median follow-up of 2.3 years (maximum, 5 years)
median_followup.location: Results, Follow-up and Effects on Clinical End Points
median_followup.note: Design paper (S5) had planned an average follow-up of 3 to 4 years.

primary_endpoint.value: Final: first nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke, cardiovascular death, or hospitalization for unstable angina that led to urgent revascularization. Original (at trial start): nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke, or cardiovascular death (MACE).
primary_endpoint.quote: At trial initiation on April 4, 2013, the primary end point was the first occurrence of a major adverse cardiovascular event (a composite of non-fatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or cardiovascular death). On January 24, 2018, after review by the NHLBI and an independent external panel, the trial end point was expanded to include hospitalization for unstable angina that led to urgent coronary revascularization; this end point would provide greater power and allow for a smaller overall sample size.
primary_endpoint.note: Endpoint expanded before unblinding of the investigators; both original and final endpoints are reported and both crossed the futility boundary.

inclusion_key_criteria.value: Age >=18; prior MI or multivessel coronary disease; plus type 2 diabetes or metabolic syndrome; medically stable; completed a 5-8 week open-label methotrexate run-in without adverse effects; no hsCRP criterion. Exclusions: chronic infection, TB, interstitial pneumonitis/pulmonary fibrosis, alcohol abuse, hepatic or renal dysfunction, NYHA IV HF, women of childbearing potential, glucocorticoids or other immunosuppressants.
inclusion_key_criteria.quote: Patients 18 years of age or older were eligible if they had a history of myocardial infarction or multivessel coronary disease and either type 2 diabetes or the metabolic syndrome.
inclusion_key_criteria.note: S1 Discussion: 'CIRT did not screen for C-reactive protein level but instead required participants to have either diabetes or the metabolic syndrome.' Design paper S5 (2013) originally specified prior MI within 5 years; S1 also allows multivessel coronary disease.

planned_events.quote: The anticipated trial sample size was reduced from 7000 to 5500, and the targeted number of primary end-point events (including the expanded definition) was increased from 530 to 634 to give the trial 90% power to detect a 23% lower rate of the primary end point in the methotrexate group than the placebo group.
planned_events.note: Original plan (public before readout, S5): 530 MACE events. Observed: 408 final-primary events (201+207) and 337 original-primary events (170+167), i.e. the trial stopped short of either target.

assumed_rrr.quote: to give the trial 90% power to detect a 23% lower rate of the primary end point in the methotrexate group than the placebo group
assumed_rrr.note: Original design (S5): 'The trial has a 90 percent power to detect a 25 percent relative hazard reduction in the primary endpoint'.

power.quote: The trial has a 90 percent power to detect a 25 percent relative hazard reduction in the primary endpoint, based on a two-sided log-rank test with alpha=0.05.
power.note: Revised plan (S1) also 90% power (for 23% RRR, 634 events).

alpha.quote: based on a two-sided log-rank test with alpha=0.05
alpha.note: S1 does not restate alpha; the original two-sided 0.05 from the design paper is used.

stopped_early.quote: However, before these changes could be fully implemented across trial operations, the data and safety monitoring board, at a meeting on March 13, 2018, recommended early termination of the trial because it had crossed a pre-specified boundary for futility for both the original and final end points and because of the lack of evidence of a reduction in C-reactive protein level with methotrexate treatment.
stopped_early.note: Stopped for futility; NHLBI accepted on April 2, 2018 ('These recommendations were accepted by the NHLBI on April 2, 2018, at which time both enrollment and efficacy follow-up ceased.'). The early stop was reported in the news in May 2018 without efficacy data (S12).

hr.note: Original primary end point (MACE): 170 vs 167; HR 1.01 (0.82-1.25), P=0.91. CV death HR 1.14 (0.76-1.72); all-cause death 96 vs 83, HR 1.16 (0.87-1.56); nonfatal MI HR 0.99 (0.76-1.29). Registry S4 reports identical HR 0.96 (0.79-1.16), p=0.67 and 1.01 (0.82-1.25), p=0.91.

safety_signals.value: Non-basal-cell skin cancer increased: 31 vs 10 (rate ratio 3.08)
safety_signals.quote: Cancers developed in more patients in the methotrexate group than in the placebo group (52 vs. 30; rate ratio, 1.72; P= 0.02), an effect that was due almost entirely to a larger number of patients with non–basal-cell skin cancer in the methotrexate group (31 vs. 10; rate ratio, 3.08; P = 0.002).
safety_signals.note: S1 Discussion calls it 'a finding that was unexpected and that merits further exploration'. With a MedDRA-based definition, any cancer 106 vs 95 (P=0.51) and non-basal-cell skin cancer 33 vs 12 (P=0.003).

safety_signals.note: Table cells joined with ' | ' by the XML-to-text conversion; columns: MTX n, rate/100 py, placebo n, rate/100 py, P.

genetics.finding: No human genetic association evidence links DHFR (methotrexate's molecular target) to coronary disease: the Open Targets DHFR - coronary artery disorder association (score 0.314) rests only on 'clinical' (0.515, drug trials) and 'literature' (0.033) datatypes, with no genetic_association datatype; the same holds for myocardial infarction (0.313, clinical only)
genetics.effect: no genetic instrument / no genetic association
genetics.note: Queried via the Open Targets GraphQL API on 2026-10-25 (current release, not a pre-readout snapshot); the clinical datatype includes methotrexate trials, possibly CIRT itself. Methotrexate's anti-inflammatory action at low dose is thought to be adenosine-mediated rather than through DHFR (S1, S5), so DHFR genetics would not capture it anyway.

genetics.finding: CRP is not causal for CHD: genetically raised CRP not associated with CHD risk (CRP CHD Genetics Collaboration, 194,418 participants)
genetics.effect: RR 1.00 (0.90-1.13) per 1 SD higher genetically raised ln CRP vs observational RR 1.33 (1.23-1.43)
genetics.quote: Human genetic data indicate that C reactive protein concentration itself is unlikely to be even a modest causal factor in coronary heart disease.
genetics.note: Abstract read on PubMed. Before readout. hsCRP is a marker of the upstream IL-1/IL-6 pathway, not a causal target.

genetics.finding: IL-6 receptor signalling is causal for CHD: IL6R Asp358Ala (rs2228145) raises IL6R and IL-6, lowers CRP, and lowers CHD risk 3.4% per allele (IL6R Genetics Consortium ERFC, 51,441 CHD cases)
genetics.quote: Large-scale human genetic and biomarker data are consistent with a causal association between IL6R-related pathways and coronary heart disease.
genetics.note: Abstract read on PubMed. Before readout. Methotrexate did not lower IL-6 in CIRT (IL-6 rose slightly), so this causal pathway was not engaged.

genetics.finding: IL6R MR Consortium (companion paper): IL6R rs7529229 associated with lower CHD odds
genetics.effect: OR 0.95 (0.93-0.97) per allele, p=1.53e-5; 25,458 cases / 100,740 controls
genetics.quote: On the basis of genetic evidence in human beings, IL6R signalling seems to have a causal role in development of coronary heart disease.
genetics.note: Abstract read on PubMed. Before readout.

consensus_explanation.summary: CIRT was stopped for futility: low-dose methotrexate did not reduce the final primary end point (201 vs 207 events; HR 0.96, 95% CI 0.79-1.16) or the original MACE end point (HR 1.01, 0.82-1.25). The investigators and later reviewers explain the null result by the pathway: unlike canakinumab in CANTOS, methotrexate did not lower IL-1beta, IL-6 or hsCRP at 8 months or over the trial (IL-6 even rose slightly), so the drug's anti-inflammatory mechanism (folate antagonism / adenosine, target DHFR, with no human genetic support in coronary disease) never engaged the IL-1beta to IL-6 to CRP pathway that genetics (IL6R Mendelian randomisation) implicates as causal. Aday and Ridker conclude that inhibiting that central pathway is 'likely a requirement' for cytokine-mediated atheroprotection and that broadly targeting inflammation may be insufficient. A contributing explanation is the population: CIRT did not select for residual inflammatory risk (median hsCRP 1.5-1.6 mg/L vs 4.2 mg/L in CANTOS), and Soehnlein and Libby suggest such patients may have stood to benefit little; Aday and Ridker note this may not fully account for the result because methotrexate did not lower inflammatory markers regardless of baseline hsCRP and there was no effect modification by baseline hsCRP. The mid-trial endpoint expansion and early stop are not considered the reason, since both endpoints crossed the futility boundary; methotrexate also increased non-basal-cell skin cancers.

pre_readout.note: readout_date 2018-11-10 (AHA Scientific Sessions presentation, simultaneous NEJM online publication S1 and Brigham press release S2). The early termination itself was public from May 2018 (S12) but without any efficacy or biomarker data.
available_before_readout: Design: 7000 patients, 530 MACE events, 90% power for a 25% RRR, two-sided alpha 0.05, no hsCRP entry criterion, diabetes or metabolic syndrome required (design paper S5, 2013-05-03; registry S4 first posted 2012-05-09)
Rationale that low-dose methotrexate lowers CRP, IL-6 and TNF-alpha in rheumatologic disease and observational RR 0.79 for CV events (cited in S5)
IL6R Asp358Ala Mendelian randomisation: IL-6 signalling causal for CHD (S7, S8, 2012-03-14)
CANTOS result (Aug 2017, external): IL-1beta inhibition lowered hsCRP/IL-6 and MACE (not a source in this file; see data/golden_set/cantos.json)
News that NHLBI stopped CIRT early on DSMB advice, 'no substantive safety concerns', results expected at AHA 2018 (S12, 2018-05-22; secondary source)
only_after_readout: HRs, events and P values for the final and original primary end points (S1, S4 results posted 2020-07-24)
Absence of any IL-1beta, IL-6 or hsCRP reduction (S1, S3 Table S2) and run-in hsCRP data (S3 Table S1)
Baseline median hsCRP 1.5-1.6 mg/L in the randomized population (S1)
Revised design (5500 patients, 634 events, 23% RRR) and the January 24, 2018 endpoint expansion as described in S1; whether these were visible in the registry history before readout was not checked
Futility reason for the DSMB recommendation (S1)
Skin cancer, liver-enzyme and leukopenia signals (S1)

open_questions: Placebo-adjusted biomarker changes are DERIVED as differences of the two arms' median changes at 8 months (Table S2); the paper gives no formal placebo-adjusted estimate or confidence interval. Annual hsCRP data (Fig. S5) were not extracted numerically.

dal-GenE was considered first: its first public results were the European Heart Journal online publication of 2022-07-20, and DalCor's press release came a day later (2022-07-21), so no press release exists on the readout day; it was skipped for that reason.
Readout date: the early stop was public in May 2018 (S12) but without efficacy data; the topline result was first public at AHA on 2018-11-10.
The press release S2 has no Wayback capture on the readout day; the earliest capture of the same page is 2019-08-25, and the live URL redirects to an unrelated page.
Whether the January 24, 2018 endpoint expansion and the revised 634-event plan were visible in the public registry before 2018-11-10 was not checked (registry history not read).

Category weighting: S1/S9 (Ridker, CIRT PI) emphasise the pathway not engaged; S10 (Soehnlein and Libby) offers the low-inflammation population as an equal alternative. The primary category target_not_causal reflects the mechanism argument; population is secondary.

Target genetics: there is no Mendelian randomisation instrument for DHFR or for methotrexate's adenosine-mediated action, so the calculator input is target_genetics 'uncertain' (no null genetic study exists). The category target_not_causal rests on the absence of genetic support for the target plus the trial's failure to engage the genetically supported IL-1beta/IL-6 pathway, as the experts argue; it is not a genetic null like darapladib/PLA2G7.
S11 (Ridker, J Intern Med 2018) was not read (paywalled).
Analyses exclude a small cluster of sites with Good Clinical Practice violations (S1 Section E, not read).
